newsitem.title: FRANCE: France hails U.N. reform plan, urges U.S.to pay up.
newsitem.headline: France hails U.N. reform plan, urges U.S.to pay up.

text.p: France on Tuesday praised U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan's 10-point proposal to make staff cuts and shave $123 million off the world body's budget, and urged the United States to pay its $1 billion arrears.
"We praise the speed with which Mr Kofi Annan has undertaken long-term reforms," France's Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
"Mr Annan has all of our support to continue in this direction, which is the right one, with reforms that will increase the efficiency of the United Nations," it added.

Under pressure from the United States to begin reforms as quickly as possible, Annan proposed cutting 1,000 permanent jobs, creating a code of conduct for U.N. employees and cutting administrative costs by the year 2001.
The measures were the first part of a reform Annan pledged to undertake when he assumed his job on January 1.
In a barely veiled reference to U.S. arrears, the ministry statement said that even with reform, the U.N. could only function effectively once all members had paid their debts.

"We emphasise that the United Nations will not be able to operate in conditions satisfying to all of its member states unless it can count on the regular, unconditional payment of obligatory contributions," it said.
The United States, which has conditioned its payments on the pace of reform, vetoed the re-election of former U.N. chief Boutros Boutros-Ghali, saying he was not implementing reform quickly enough.
The U.S. veto further strained relations with France, which had campaigned to keep Boutros-Ghali in office.
